read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page frozen PDF, including references and Appendices A–G; visually inspected all pages, Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–11. Read paper.tex and the complete included results source, consulted the component-table source and the frozen example-selection manifest for presentation/provenance details. Treated technical appendices as optional depth when judging main-text accessibility. Read only the fixed rubric and this frozen manuscript package; no earlier drafts, other reviews, progress records or external sources were used. Extraction and renders were isolated under /tmp/editorial_r19_b_pdf. The PDF SHA256 was independently computed.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with manageable paragraphs and useful interpretive sentences. Section 4.1 explains contrasts through the actual Monet–Sisley lightness difference before introducing notation, and Section 5.4 plainly explains why shrinking can reduce total error while weakening aligned response. Terminology distinguishes alignment, mismatch, collection proximity and perceived resemblance consistently. Only a small amount of removable main-text repetition remains, particularly the energy/proximity qualification in Section 4.4 whose numerical results are deferred entirely to the appendix.
score_reasons.structure: The paper progresses coherently from the question and controlled arms to features, intuitive score definitions, primary results and retrospective explanations. Sections 5.1–5.5 have informative headings; the primary family, calibration and source audit remain visibly distinct. Detailed identities, control simulations and earlier cohorts are appropriately optional. The main structural refinement is to relocate the short energy-discrepancy introduction beside its appendix results so that the main methods retain their two-score focus.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract stands alone, identifies the sample and reference target, and states the principal results with their limits. The six prompt conditions, equal painter weighting, development-IQR units, repeat correction, D=1 theoretical benchmark and meaning of calibration are explained without repository consultation. Tables 2–4 make the inferential and descriptive comparisons interpretable. Figures 1–3 provide useful complementary views. A localized accessibility opportunity is to identify the four pictured historical works with readable titles instead of only opaque work IDs.
score_reasons.engagement: The consequential distinction between a visible name response and correct painter differences sustains a clear narrative. Figure 1 invites direct inspection, the M/S/P detail views in Figure 2 reveal a pattern hidden by the overall projection, and Table 3 makes the calibration and scene-averaging reversals concrete. The text consistently explains what numerical findings reveal without hype. The short detour into an appendix-only metric and the impersonal reference-image identifiers slightly reduce an otherwise strong pace and visual connection to the paintings.

strengths: Sections 1 and 4.1 use the Monet–Sisley comparison to explain why generic movement toward paintings cannot establish painter-specific agreement; the numerical lightness example makes centering concrete.
The main text separates aligned response from total mismatch with the no-distinction/exact/doubled examples, then uses GPT Image 2 and FLUX to demonstrate the distinction in actual results.
Figure 1 shows every experimental arm for every model with an explicit selection rule, while its caption clearly states that the historical examples were neither inputs nor matched compositions.
The source-correction result is not buried: Section 5.1 flags the changed comparison, Section 5.5 explains it, and Table 4 shows both intervals alongside the retrospective qualification.
Section 5.4 explains the calibration and scene-averaging ordering changes through their substantive meaning, and explicitly avoids claiming statistical superiority or improved images.
Uncertainty, the finite digital target, AI-only source auditing and incomplete exact-pixel access are stated candidly; technical appendix depth does not obstruct the standalone main argument.

findings.location: Section 4.4, page 6; Section 5.2, page 8; Appendix E, pages 18–19
findings.issue: Section 4.4 introduces energy discrepancy as an additional metric, including its interpretation and two appendix references, but the main results provide no energy values and Section 5.2 merely redirects the reader to Appendix E. This is a small methods detour with no main-text payoff.
findings.reader_effect: A new reader may devote attention to retaining a third score while the central argument depends on aligned response and error. It briefly weakens the otherwise clear hierarchy of primary and complementary measurements.
findings.suggested_change: Keep the sentence explaining the two control arms in Section 4.4, and move the energy definition and its formula pointers to the opening of Appendix E, where the collection-level numbers are reported. Retain the short Appendix E pointer in Section 5.2. Consolidate overlapping appendix wording so all evidence is preserved without increasing the 22-page manuscript.

findings.location: Figure 1, page 4; Appendix D, page 18; frozen example_selection.json reference entries
findings.issue: The reference thumbnails are labeled only with Wikidata Q-identifiers. Neither their caption nor Appendix D names the four works, although their titles are available in the supplied figure manifest.
findings.reader_effect: The images remain useful experimental illustrations, but a reader cannot identify the historical examples or connect them to their subjects without leaving the manuscript. This modestly limits the figure’s engagement and standalone inspectability.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the ID-only thumbnail labels with short readable title labels drawn from the existing manifest, such as “Rocks at Port-Goulphar” and “River Oise near Pontoise”; retain the complete titles and Q-identifiers in the manifest. Use the existing label area and abbreviated titles so the figure and manuscript do not grow.

summary: An excellent and largely self-contained editorial presentation of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main findings and the limits of their interpretation are readily recoverable, and the retrospective results are clearly identified. Remaining improvements are localized: remove an appendix-only metric detour from the main methods and make the historical examples easier to identify. No consequential claim-fidelity problem was found within the supplied manuscript.
